draft.title: Atoms and elements
card: An atom is a very small particle that makes up all matter. Atoms are the building blocks of every substance.
An element is a substance made of only one type of atom. Gold is an element because it contains only gold atoms.
All known elements are set out in the periodic table, each shown by its symbol. An element cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reactions.
Each element has a symbol of one or two letters, such as O for oxygen and Fe for iron. The first letter is a capital and the second is lower case.
draft.remember: An element has one type of atom only, and it has its own symbol.

a.q: A student says copper is an element. What makes this true?
opts: It is made of only one type of atom
It is made of atoms joined in a fixed ratio
It is a mixture of metals with similar atoms
It can be broken down into simpler substances
a.why: An element is a substance made of only one type of atom, and copper contains only copper atoms. Atoms joined in a fixed ratio describes something else, because an element does not need different atoms joined together. An element also cannot be broken down into simpler substances.
a.clue: Think about how many types of atom an element contains.

b.q: Sam is labelling a jar of iron. Its symbol comes from the letters f and e. How should he write the symbol?
opts: Fe, with a capital F and a lower case e
FE, with both letters as capitals
fe, with both letters in lower case
fE, with a lower case f and a capital E
b.why: A symbol starts with a capital letter, and any second letter is lower case, so iron is Fe. FE is the most tempting wrong option, but it breaks the rule that the second letter is lower case.
b.clue: Only one letter in a symbol is a capital. Which one?

a.best: It is made of only one type of atom

b.best: Fe, with a capital F and a lower case e
